title: Mochin DeTzelem, Vol. 12: Show, Don’t Tell
subtitle: How Chazal encode Torah, and the axis of Amidah and Nefilah, life and death.
html:
From Mikraei Kodesh, the Torah writings collected on liorsollyshachar.com.

מבוא א': א, ב, ג, ד

Part 1

Prologue:

Chazal have a style of communicating Torah shebaal peh that requires acclimation. One element of that style is what some circles refer to as “show don't tell.” This means that if you want to get something across, it’s artistically preferable not to say but to demonstrate the thing. The clothing in which an idea is disclosed is one selection out of many because the same idea might have been dressed up in another way. If you share the vision of reality that the communicator is operating with, the choice of clothing is a negligible boundary; all you need is the mere tracing of the silhouette to fill in the blanks yourself1. Besides for the efficiency of encoding higher planes of information across massive webs of resonance and isomorphism already present in the substrate of pshat and midrashim, this model acts to protect the secrets. The same sleeping document can be passed down with a level coherence that maintains its fidelity because it is saying something logical on its own revealed level, while still carrying within it an encoded web of the total picture for those who want to mine for it. It is a sleeping document until it arrives at every single person. Your chelek in Torah has been asleep, and yet present in every single generations’ copy of Shas Bavli, awaiting your eventual discovery of the personal within those same pages. A secret is not something that is not being said, it is something that cannot be said because it is the prelinguistic gestalt of your consciousness as a neshamah which is the unique project you contribute to the totality.

Another benefit of Torah’s medium is that by design, you are forced to rearticulate the same reality in totally different language through the ever-shifting veils of context. Divrei Torah are tzadku yachdav, they are truest when seen together, and at times ani bemakom echad, poor in revelatory valence, only to be revealed as ashir, a massive bank of clarity from which you can cash out, somewhere else. It is for this reason that Chazal’s method of fragmentation forces us to take all the information we are given and keep every synonym stacked simultaneously in our field of view. The variety of Being can be unified in one discussion because there are never truly different things, there is only always one.

Consider the notion of ‘Nefilah’ in Chochmat HaTorah. It’s not a term only used in reference to downward motion; any collapse of structure is a Nefilah. So immediately, we have a spectral axis, literally a middah2, spanning from the top which is Amidah, a system who’s structure is robust and integral, down to the bottom, which is the polarity of Nefilah, where the system is dis-integrated, fallen. The greatest example of this is a stillbirth which is called a nefel. The antonymous adjective of nefel is kayam, i.e. a child that made it through birth is Zera Shel Kayama, kiyum relating to endurance, persistence, being alive, coherent, structurally sound. Kayam it turns out relates to the term Amad, as in kum, get up, get up and now you are standing, meumad, which is the mochin of Chabad, which means you are not yoshev, which is mochin of Chagat, or shochev, which is mochin of Nahi, or heaven forbid, totally nishbar where there are no mochin at all, only rapach hevel degarmi because you’ve fallen into Bya from Atzilut, or in other words, Died, the ultimate nap. Succinctly, the dimension of Amidah-Nefilah describes the condition of a system: on the top we have Meumad, Kayam, and on the bottom, we have Naful, Nishbar, not kayam. These two polarities were introduced to us as Me’umad and Naful, but there is a more general duality that maps to the core of this spectral axis, i.e. Middah, of Life and Death.

As alluded to, Chachamim define death in relation to the Zayin Malchei Edom, where total disintegration means that the thing is no longer alive. These Melachim died because of disintegration, which informs us that it's antonym, Life, is found through integration, relationship, coherent structure and unity. If being Maamid the Olam means working to bring the world closer to the state about which we could use the adjective Alive in describing it, i.e., to bring our Olam from an Olam of Death and Pirud3 to an Olam of Life and Dvekut, then we want to know how to stand up the world. It turns out that the original necessity of a process for standing the world up was birthed with conception of death, the effect caused by the Chet of Adam. Therefore, the tikun, which is our responsibility within the process, is to be Ma’amid the Olam, which must have something to do with integration and relationship towards life, re-viving, i.e., resurrection, i.e. techiyat hametim (and by the way, like we find by the bracha of Techiyat HaMetim in Shmona Esre, the metim are in reference to rapach!).

  1. There are two kinds of tzadikim, like we find in Shaar Maamrei Zohar. Some speak clearly and openly, and others are masters at speaking through an inner conversation, through only the second of the double entendres, enlightening those in the crowd that know and leaving those that don’t know with either nothing, confusion, or in a worst-case scenario, with the illusion that they understood. The reason why the Rashbi was chosen to megale the Zohar was not because he was the greatest in the generation in that space but because he was the greatest in the latter middah.↩︎

  2. Any dimension is a spectrum along an axis. The ones we’re used to of height and depth etc are marked with arbitrary, equidistant magnitudes on a ruler are examples of some dimensions but not all dimensions. With those rulers, essentialy we are now able to say how much within this dimension. But a dimension can be something like color, where the measure is in wavelengths of light. You can have a dimension of Italianness and put all the supermarket spaghettis along the axis line, with Barilla perhaps as a middle point to ground the scale in stable relativity. So the anatomy of a dimension is way before space, it emerges as soon as you have a spectrum through which you can coordinate something. And even after space, you don’t need space to coordinate most of the things you see. Those spaghettis are situated within multiple dimensions at once like how many carbohydrates per serving in relation to their neighbors, while at the same time reaching as far as the dimensions of ethics and supply chains, as in, was this pasta ethically sources and were any Italians hurt in the making of this lunch? The question you should be asking is not what this pasta is, but what dimensions this pasta is situated within, and thus you retroactively discover a far more complex object than you previously thought possible.↩︎

  3. You should know that the difference between Atzilut and Briah (+ yetzira and asiyah, the three together called Alma DePiruda) is only distance. Atzilut is etzel, i.e., ihu vegarmohi chad behon, the kelim are batel to the Ohr and the whole thing is begeder Elokut. The process of making a Nivrah, i.e. a differentiated Other, is a process of distancing. Nivrah means outside, as in Bar, which is Briah. This is why the ohr toch raglei ack needed to come back only through a masach, and the entire ohr of atzilut needs to pass through another masach just to get to briah. This wasn’t needed for atzilut, it was for briah. Alma Depiruda refers to the olamot of Briya Yetzira Asyiah, with terminal perud being the spatio-temporaly alienated Olam HaZe HaGashmi. This is Yesh, that is Yotze from Ayin. The goal is to bring Yesh back to Ayin, to mevatel the yesh like wax in front of a candle. This is the dvekut at the level of atzilut, which is the tikun for all the nifradim in olamot of briah.↩︎
